correctness.rationale: Li's 1/24 almost-all short-interval theorem gives arbitrary fixed logarithmic savings for the total length of prime gaps longer than p^theta when theta>1/24. Keeping theta symbolic in Chojecki's raw-witness and forest estimates gives a raw exponent 1/2+6theta and a maximal total short-gap exponent 1/2+8theta; both forest path families decrease after their first relevant scale for 1/24<theta<1/16. Hence the short loss is X^(5/6+epsilon), and combining it with long gaps yields the stated defect bound.

originality.rationale: The inspected Chojecki preprint states a 9/10 short-gap exponent at theta=1/20 and only a qualitative density-one final conclusion. The inspected Li manuscript gives the 1/24 prime-interval input but no application to distinct consecutive products. Searches of exact and synonymous formulations did not locate the 5/6-plus-epsilon short-loss estimate or the all-log-powers global defect estimate. Recent concurrent work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades density one to a quantitative complement bound beating every fixed logarithmic proportion for the same canonical construction and sharpens the structured short-gap exponent from 9/10 to 5/6 plus epsilon. The parameterized forest calculation also makes the dependence on future almost-all prime-gap improvements explicit.
